title: Optimizing the Input Pipeline knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Parallel data loading” in this lesson?
options: This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
questions.answer_key: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.
questions.explanation: Parallel data loading: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Memory pinning”, what should a learner verify?
options: reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
questions.answer_key: reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Batch-size tuning”?
options: Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
questions.answer_key: Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
